title: Web Typography: A handbook for designing beautiful and effective typography in responsive websites
authority: Rutter is a long-time UK web designer, co-founder of Clearleft and Fontdeck and creator of webtypography.net, the web adaptation of Bringhurst's rules.
caveats: Publication month varies across listings (Jan to May 2017). CSS features have moved on since (clamp, font-optical-sizing, size-adjust), so check browser support before copying code.

title: On Web Typography
authority: Santa Maria is a designer, co-founder of A Book Apart and founder of Typedia, writing from design practice for web designers.
caveats: Practitioner judgement, not experimental research. Reflects 2014 browser capabilities. Listings differ on page count and ISBN.

title: More Meaningful Typography
authority: Brown is a type designer and later head of typography at Adobe/Typekit; this article popularized modular scales on the web.
caveats: Harmonic ratios are an aesthetic heuristic with no experimental support that they improve reading. Sizes in the article assume pixel and em units of 2011.

title: Flexible Typesetting
authority: Brown was head of typography at Adobe Typekit and a long-standing authority on responsive and scale-based type; foreword by Jessica Hische.
caveats: Practitioner framework, not experimental research. Examples predate widespread clamp() and variable-font use.

title: Web Design is 95% Typography
authority: Reichenstein is founder of iA (iA Writer) and a widely cited voice in screen reading typography and responsive type.
caveats: The 95% figure is rhetorical, not measured; the author later said he knew little typography then and preferred a different title. Weak for image, video or interaction-heavy design.

title: Butterick's Practical Typography
authority: Butterick is a typographer and type designer (Hermes, Equity, Concourse) who also practices law; the book is a widely used professional guide.
caveats: Opinionated; numbers are rules of thumb from practice. First-publication year is approximate. Fonts discussed are mostly paid fonts.

title: Webfont Handbook
authority: Stein worked at Adobe Typekit and wrote the Font Face Observer library; the handbook is the standard practical reference on webfont delivery.
caveats: Some listings say 2016 but the publisher page gives 2017. Loading APIs (font-display, size-adjust) have developed since.

title: A Comprehensive Guide to Font Loading Strategies
authority: Leatherman is a front-end developer who documented and named the font loading strategies (FOUT, FOIT, FOFT) used in production.
caveats: Guide is regularly updated; check the live version. Browser behavior of font-display and preload has changed since 2017.

title: Precise control over responsive typography
authority: Riethmuller is an established front-end developer whose calc() interpolation formula became the basis of most fluid type systems.
caveats: Exact publication year to be confirmed (appeared on his site before wider write-ups in 2016). Pure viewport-unit sizing defeats browser zoom; clamp() with rem is now preferred.

title: The details of UI typography (WWDC20 session 10175) and Human Interface Guidelines: Typography
authority: Official documentation by the designers of San Francisco, the system font of Apple platforms; describes optical sizing and Dynamic Type.
caveats: Platform guidance for native apps; point values do not map directly to CSS pixels. HIG pages change over time.

title: Material Design 3: Typography
authority: Official type system of the most widely deployed UI design system; defines roles, sizes and line heights as tokens.
caveats: Counts of styles vary across variants (baseline 15, Expressive adds emphasized roles); year is approximate for Material You. Exact values should be checked on the official page.

title: CSS Fonts Module Level 3
edition: Level 4 and 5 add optical sizing, variable axes, font-display, size-adjust
authority: The web standard defining @font-face, font-variant-numeric, font-feature-settings and related properties.
caveats: Recommendation status date is from memory; search confirmed Level 3 CR 2013 and 2018. Features such as font-display, font-optical-sizing and size-adjust are in Level 4 and 5 working drafts.

title: Thinking with Type: A critical guide for designers, writers, editors, and students
authority: Lupton is a designer, curator at Cooper Hewitt and director of a graphic design program; the book is a standard university text.
caveats: Print-centered, with limited treatment of web delivery; later editions add screen material.

title: Stop Stealing Sheep & Find Out How Type Works
authority: Spiekermann is co-founder of FontShop, designer of FF Meta and Fira Sans, with decades in signage and screen type.
caveats: Co-author attribution differs by edition (Ginger on 1993 and 2002 editions; 3rd edition credits Spiekermann). First edition publisher listed variously as Adobe Press or Peachpit.

title: Typeface features and legibility research
authority: Bigelow co-designed Lucida and the Wingdings and is a MacArthur Fellow; the review connects vision science and type design.
caveats: Review of mixed-quality older studies; many classic claims about serifs are untested. Abstract not retrieved this session, so the notes rely on prior knowledge and should be re-checked.
